findings.failure_scenario: swissknifeman doctor with no arguments runs <provides.cli[0]> doctor for every non-bridge unit that declares provides.doctor, in id order: bin/aicore, bin/analyst, bin/brain, bin/harness, bin/maind, packages/orch/scripts/orch.py, bin/skiller. bin/aicore doctor is not a command: aicore.cli.main(["doctor"]) returns 2 and writes "aicore: unknown group 'doctor'". doctor_command does rc = code or rc, so a later exit 0 leaves the umbrella exit at 2. The previous launcher exec'd only skiller, harness, maind, and analyst, in that order, each as <launcher> doctor. item.rules[3] and hub-p12 rule 3 require that same exec. The scope leaves the new doctor aggregator to P12.2 and forbids a doctor stub in P12.1. scripts/test-umbrella.py TestLegacyGroups never compares this argv, and test_doctor_fan_out only checks fake echo CLIs, so V1 stays green.

Observed the seven targets above and exit 2 with 'aicore: unknown group doctor'.

findings.failure_scenario: swissknifeman planner-orch and swissknifeman orch-skiller both return exit 1 and 'Unknown command', and exec nothing. Their unit.json provides.cli entries are brief.py and resolve_role.py. group_units drops kind bridge, so route never execs <root>/<provides.cli[0]> plus the remaining arguments. The umbrella routing rule says an id with provides.cli is that command. Help uses the same filter, so both ids are absent from the module list. orch-harness has an empty provides and stays unknown, which matches the rule.
